title: Giving Instructions: Do This!
summary: Learn how to use imperative verbs to tell people what to do. You will practice giving simple directions and commands.

sections.p: We use imperatives to tell someone to do something. They are very direct. You just use the base form of the verb. You do not need to add words like 'you'. For example, instead of saying 'You open the door', you just say 'Open the door'. We use imperatives for recipes, street directions, and classroom rules.

ex.mean: ask someone to make the window open
tell someone to take a seat
pay attention to the person speaking

sections.p: To tell someone NOT to do something, we put 'Don't' before the verb. 'Don't' is short for 'Do not'. It is very useful for safety rules and warnings. You can use it at home, at work, or on the street.

ex.mean: do not put your hands on the hot pan
leaving your car in this spot is not allowed

sections.p: Imperatives can sometimes sound a little strong. To be polite, we usually add the word 'please' at the beginning or the end of the sentence. Adding 'please' makes people happy to help you.

ex.en: Please help me with this bag.

ex.mean: a polite request to make the room dark

tip: Think of recipe books or video games. They always use short action words to tell you what to do next!

quiz.en: ___ the door, it is cold outside.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct verb for a recipe

quiz.en: ___ feed the animals at the zoo.
